summary: WP-002 implementation was already present in EpisodeListPage.php. Verified all requirements:
R1: ep_page read from request via $this->request->getParam('ep_page')
R2: $params array built conditionally — only set when epPage is not null
R5: Comic::getURLEpisodeList(array $params=array()) already accepts optional params
PHPStan analysis passed with 0 errors (138 files analysed)

comments.note: In handleRefreshDetails(), the ep_page parameter is cast to (int) but is stored as a mixed type in $params. This is fine functionally, but a type annotation on $params (array<string, int>) would make the intent clearer.
The grid-actions CSS block is inlined as a <style> tag inside _render(). In a larger codebase this would be better in the external app.css, but for a local tool this is acceptable.

summary: All 4 acceptance criteria verified against the source code in EpisodeListPage.php.
Build check: PHPStan reports 0 errors across 138 files.
Regression: 60/60 PHPUnit tests pass (1 pre-existing skip, 1 pre-existing deprecation).
AC1: handleRefreshDetails() reads ep_page from request, builds $params conditionally, passes to success redirect via getURLEpisodeList($params). Confirmed in source.
AC2: Same $params used for error redirect — both branches use getURLEpisodeList($params). Confirmed in source.
AC3: When ep_page is null, $params stays empty → no ep_page in redirect URL (pre-existing behaviour). When on page 1, hidden form posts ep_page=1 → redirect includes ep_page=1 (AC allows this).
AC4: Comic::getURLEpisodeList() unconditionally re-sets page=EpisodeList and comicID after merging the caller's params — both are always preserved.
Edge cases reviewed: non-numeric ep_page cast to int (0) normalises on reload; missing ep_page falls back to page 1 correctly.

comments.note: Edge case: if a crafted POST sends a non-numeric ep_page, the (int) cast produces 0, resulting in ep_page=0 in the redirect URL. ArrayPagination normalises this to page 1 on the next render, so no functional harm. Risk is negligible for a local/LAN tool.
No improvement: Code is clean and consistent with project conventions.

summary: Code review complete. Implementation in EpisodeListPage::handleRefreshDetails() is correct, minimal, and secure. All 5 requirements met, all 4 ACs satisfied.

Params array is built once before both redirect branches — no duplication risk. (int) cast on ep_page sanitizes user-supplied input before it reaches buildURL(). Comic::getURLEpisodeList() hard-overwrites page= and comicID= after merging caller params, guaranteeing AC4 by design.
No blocking issues found. Two low-priority non-blocking observations recorded in comments.

comments.note: EpisodeListPage.php – $epPage remains typed as 'mixed' (the return type of getParam()). The (int) cast is only applied at the $params assignment. A typed local assignment — $epPage = (int)$this->request->getParam('ep_page') — combined with a !== 0 guard (or keeping the null-path) would make intent clearer. Purely cosmetic for a local tool; not a blocking concern.

ep_page=0 edge case: a non-numeric POST value is silently cast to 0, producing ep_page=0 in the redirect URL. ArrayPagination normalises this to page 1 on the next render. Benign for a LAN tool, and correctly flagged by QA. No action required.
No blocking issues. Code is clean, idiomatic, and consistent with project conventions.
